_comment: EXAMPLE ONLY -- this is the TEMPLATE copy, showing the shape a real case's manifest takes. Do NOT hand-edit a real one: generate it with `python tools/binary_archive_manifest.py --generate`, which reads each archive directory's PROVENANCE.txt, and check it with `--verify` (M1-M7). The binaries themselves are NOT in git -- hundreds of MB each, and not regenerable, since a recompile can perturb floating point and a rebuilt binary is a different artifact. This file is the record that they existed and the checksum to prove one has not been altered or swapped.
_how_to_use: 1. Archive the built executable under $A2MC_BINARY_ARCHIVE_ROOT/<label>/ beside a PROVENANCE.txt.
2. PROVENANCE.txt fields are parsed ONE PER LINE -- a wrapped value is silently truncated. Recognised: SHA256, Case, Build dir, Source, Change, Archived, Why, V0 pair.
3. Run --generate to write this file, then --verify before trusting the ledger.

4. Record the claim in calibration_rounds.yaml at rounds[N].fates_source.binary = {archive_label, sha256_prefix}; check M7 cross-checks it and PRINTS how many claims it checked, so a pass over zero claims is visible.

archives.label: R1_<descriptor>_<short_commit>
archives.sha256: <64 hex chars, computed from the archived file>
archives.provenance_sha256: <the SHA256 line inside PROVENANCE.txt; must equal sha256, or M3 errors>
archives.built_in_case: <the CIME case directory the build ran in>
archives.source: <what the code was: model version / commit, and the branch or patch it carries>
archives.change: <what this build changes, and whether the switch is default-off>
